narrative.overview:
The whole app is one striped candy box. A board is a tray with compartments, and every move drops a candy into one of them. A red and milk awning sits on top, the mint field runs edge to edge, and a chameleon on a branch tells the player the one thing to do next. It is cheerful, cute and physical, built for a phone held in one hand during a short break.

Density follows the game: lobbies are loose and friendly, while play screens give almost all their height to the board and pin the tools under the thumb. The material language is thick plum ink outlines, milk trays, and hard candy with soft shadows. Decoration never slows or covers play.

The system rejects the standard game app of white cards on a grey ground.
keyCharacteristics: Mint dotted field across the full screen, no neutral grey anywhere
Thick plum outlines (3 to 5px) on every tray, candy and control
Soft shadows plus one streak of gloss as the only depth
Springy drops as the signature motion, with reduced motion respected
Teal for you, lemon for rivals, red for conflict during Sudoku versus
One chameleon line per screen, in Vietnamese

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: Two reds ship on purpose. Mascot art keeps Mascot Stripe Red; everything in the UI uses Candy Cherry so milk text passes contrast. Never swap one for the other to tidy the palette.

rules.name: The Whose Candy Rule
rules.body: On the Sudoku versus board and progress bars, teal means you, lemon means rivals, and red means only a conflict. This is scoped to that play surface: Candy Cherry stays the primary action colour elsewhere and is the X piece in Caro.

rules.name: The Ink Channel Rule
rules.body: Ink with alpha must go through the rgb channel token `--ink-rgb` (85 48 63), which is what makes Tailwind opacity modifiers work on `ink`. A hex custom property cannot take an alpha modifier.

rules.name: The Readable Vào Rule
rules.body: A display face must have a Vietnamese subset and a V that cannot be read as U. Coiny was rejected because its V broke "Vào". Test any replacement on real Vietnamese UI words, not on the name of the app.

rules.name: The Grid Truth Rule
rules.body: Lines and digits sit dead straight. Sudoku 3x3 box lines live on their own overlay layer so cell borders never cut them, and digits use tabular figures. Playfulness belongs to the candy, not the grid.

rules.name: The One Streak Rule
rules.body: Depth is a soft shadow and a single streak of gloss in white at 65 to 70%. Never use hard offset shadows or rim bevels. This is a candy, not a sticker or a plastic key.

rules.name: The One Wrapper Rule
rules.body: The wrapped candy is reserved for the main action of a screen. If two candies seem to qualify, one of them is an outline button.

rules.name: The One Line Rule
rules.body: Each screen has exactly one mascot line: an imperative or reaction in a milk speech bubble with an ink tail. A dialog is its own layer and may speak for itself, and status captions such as loading or paused labels are not lines.

rules.name: The Always There Rule
rules.body: At short heights the mascot gets smaller and never disappears, down to 40px wide beside the board at 720px tall or less.

rules.name: The Given Ink Rule
rules.body: Given digits stay plain ink. Player digits are dropped candies, 84% of the cell, with an arc of gloss. The candy falls from above on a bouncy spring (620/17) and turns cherry on conflict. Conflict follows Sudoku rules only, never the answer, because versus clients do not hold the solution.

rules.name: The Two Signals Rule
rules.body: X is a red candy with a milk cross and O is a teal candy with a milk ring, so pieces differ by shape as well as colour. Keep both signals in any new piece treatment. Pieces drop with a spring (560/15); the last move sits on Lemon Cream, and winning cells turn lemon with their candies bouncing.

rules.name: The Honest Rematch Rule
rules.body: The versus result primary is the wrapped candy "Chơi ván mới", and it goes to the game's lobby, because the server cannot restart a finished room. Never label it as an instant rematch. Practice can start again in place, so its primary is "Chơi ván nữa".

dos: Do build every new screen as milk trays with ink outlines on the mint dotted field.
Do use Candy Cherry for all UI red and keep Mascot Stripe Red inside mascot art.
Do keep teal for you, lemon for rivals and red for conflict on the Sudoku versus board and progress bars.
Do make Caro pieces differ by shape as well as colour.
Do keep given digits plain ink and make player digits dropped candies.
Do give each screen exactly one mascot line, and shrink the mascot rather than removing it at short heights.
Do test a new display face on Vietnamese words such as "Vào".
Do pair bouncy springs with `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` and the reduced-motion CSS guard.
donts: Don't use hard offset shadows or rim bevels; depth is a soft shadow plus one streak of gloss.
Don't put milk text on Mascot Stripe Red.
Don't use red on the Sudoku versus board for anything except a conflict.
Don't promise an instant rematch from a finished versus room; "Chơi ván mới" goes to the lobby.
Don't bring back the mascot's headphones or sound-wave bars.
Don't build white cards on a grey ground. Compartments live inside one tray and hold their game's real pieces.
